09-01.html:
On this day the church celebrates the birth of the pure Virgin St. Mary, the Mother of God (Theotokos), through whom mankind was saved.

In Judea there was a man whose name was Joachim with his wife Anna from the tribe of Judah, and from the house of David. They were both righteous before God walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. And in His law they meditated day and night. Anna was barren and they prayed constantly entreating God to grant them offspring. They vowed to God that if He granted them a son or a daughter, they would offer the child to the Lord to serve and dwell in the temple as Samuel the prophet.

In the fullness of time, according to the Divine Will, the angel of the Lord was sent to announce to Joachim while he was on the mountain praying for forty days: “The Lord will give you offspring through whom will be the salvation of the world.”

Immediately he went down the mountain believing what the angel told him, and he told his wife Anna what he saw and heard. She rejoiced, gave thanks to the Lord and told him that the angel had announced to her also that her petition was accepted and she will conceive and give birth to a blessed daughter. All generations will call her blessed for through her will come the salvation of Adam and his offspring.

Joachim and his wife went to the temple and while they were praying, he witnessed a crown of light coming down upon him from heaven, and his soul was consoled. He and his wife went home rejoicing. Anna spent the days of her pregnancy in fasting and prayers until she gave birth to the Mother of God, the Savior of the world, and called her Mary.

The blessing of her holy intercession be with us all, and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-01.title: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary the Mother of God

09-02.html:
On this day the righteous Job departed. He was a righteous man in his generation, as the Holy Bible testified about him: “... there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil?” (Job 1:8) The devil envied him and asked God to have authority over Job and all his possessions. God allowed that, because of His foreknowledge of the patience of Job and that he would be an example for those who would come after him as St. James said: “You have heard of the perseverance of Job and seen the end intended by the Lord” (James 5:11).

In one day, Job lost his sons and daughters, his cattle, and all his wealth. In addition, the evil one also struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his feet to the crown of his head. In all these things Job offered thanksgiving to God and did not murmur or blaspheme against his Creator. All that he said was: “May the day perish on which I was born” (Job 3:3). He also said about the loss of his children: “The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD. In all this, Job did not sin nor charge God with wrong.” (Job 1:21-22)

The thing that hurt Job the most was the admonishment given by his wife and his friends. His wife advised him to blaspheme, but Job rebuked her, saying, “`You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we indeed accept good from God, and shall we not accept adversity?’ In all this Job did not sin with his lips” (Job 2:10).

Job remained down on the ground until he was purified as gold is purified with fire. At last the Lord spoke to him from the clouds and healed him from his sickness and doubled the wealth that he had and gave him other sons and daughters. He lived to a good old age and departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-02.title: The Departure of the Righteous Job

09-02.html:
On this day also of the year 91 of the martyrs (375 A.D.), St. Tadros (Theodore) of Tabennisis, the disciple of St. Pachom the father of the monastic Koinonia, departed. He was born around the year 323 A.D. in the city of Latopolis (Esna) to a noble wealthy religious family. He manifested since his young age his inclination toward the life of piety and asceticism. At the age of twelve he went to a small monastery in nearby Esna where he worshipped in seclusion. He grew in spiritual stature.

When he heard about St. Pachom he longed to be one of his children. When he was thirteen years old the Lord willed for him to go to Abba Pachom. A monk came to the monastery where Tadros resided and Tadros asked him to take him to Abba Pachomius.

St. Pachom had prophesied that a young man would come to the monastery who would be his successor in directing the monasteries after him. When Tadros came to Abba Pachomius, he accepted him into the monastery. When he saw his obedience and his intense striving in the virtuous life, he chose him to be his close disciple.

After a while Abba Pachom appointed him as an abbot for the monastery at Tabenne when he was only twenty-four years old. When St. Tadros proved to be successful in running the monastery, St. Pachomius asked him to come to the main monastery at Pafau (Pabau) to be close to him. He also appointed him as an overseer for all the Pachomian monasteries. He visited the brethren, healed the maladies of their souls and accepted those seeking the monastic life. He was known for his gentleness and cheerful face; therefore, he was loved and respected by everyone.

He continued in all the days of his father Pachomius to be his right hand and his obedient son. After the departure of his teacher, Petronius became the general abbot of all the cenobitic monasteries for a short period of time, then departed. He was succeeded by Horsiesius who was fond of Abba Tadros. When a great dispute arose and threatened a schism among the monasteries, Horsiesius prudently assigned the general control of the communities into Theodore’s hands because of his wisdom and discernment. Tadros accepted, after much urging, to be placed under the guidance of Fr. Horsiesius.

After a short while St. Tadros became ill, so he gathered all the abbots of the monasteries and asked for their forgiveness. All the brethren wept and Fr. Horsiesius was sorrowful. He asked for their prayers and departed to paradise. His departure caused much sorrow and had a great effect on all the Pachomian monasteries.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-02.title: The Departure of St. Tadros (Theodore) of Tabennisis, the Disciple of St. Pachomius

09-02.html:
On this day also of the year 1096 of the martyrs (1380 A.D.), St. Philotheos was martyred. He was a native of “Doronka” in the province of Assuit. He was severely tormented without denying his faith and finally he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-02.title: The Martyrdom of St. Philotheos

09-03.html:
On this day St. Jason, one of the seventy disciples, departed.

He was born in Tarsus and was related to the apostle St. Paul. He ministered with the disciples before the Passion of the Savior, and performed many signs and wonders. He received the grace of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost.

After St. Paul had embraced Christianity, he went with him to Tarsus in the period from 37 A.D. to 42 A.D., and journeyed with him to many countries. Then he went to the city of Thessalonica and he made his livelihood making tents. Then he went to Rome where he preached the good news of salvation. For this reason, St. Paul sent Jason’s greeting to the people of Rome when he wrote his epistle to the Romans.

When St. Paul arrived to Thessalonica in about the year 51 A.D., he was received in Jason’s home. He worked with him in tent making so he would not be a burden on him as he mentioned in his epistle, saying, “For you remember, brethren, our labor and toil; for laboring night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you, we preached to you the gospel of God.” When St. Paul went to the synagogue of the Jews in Thessalonica, the Jews arose against him. However, he went to the house of Jason. When they did not find Paul, they dragged Jason and some brethren to the ruler of the city accusing Paul with treason and dissension. He was arrested and when they had received a guarantee from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

After St. Paul had left the city, Jason continued in his ministry. He faced many difficulties which St. Paul mentioned, saying, “For you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, just as they did from the Judeans.” “So that we ourselves boast of you among the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that you endure.”

When St. Paul was in Corinth, Jason sent him financial help. St. Paul spent the winter of the year 57 A.D. in Corinth at the end of his third missionary journey and from there he sent his epistle to the Romans in the early part of the year 58 A.D. In his epistle he sent the greetings of Jason which indicates that Jason had arrived in Corinth before the writing of the epistle to the Romans.

St. Paul ordained St. Jason bishop for his hometown Tarsus where he had preached before with the apostle Paul. He shepherded the church of Christ in Tarsus with the best of care.

Later on he preached the Gospel also in the city of Corfu (Korkiras) where many believed at his hands. He baptized them and built for them a church in the name of St. Stephen the Archdeacon and protomartyr. When the Governor of the city knew this, he imprisoned him. He found seven thieves in prison, taught them the faith and baptized them. They confessed their faith in the Lord Christ openly before the Governor who put them in boiling pitch, and, thus, they received the crowns of martyrdom.

Later on the Governor brought St. Jason out of prison, and tortured him, but he was not harmed. The daughter of the Governor was watching from her window the torture and miracles that took place and she believed in the Lord Christ, the God of St. Jason. She took off her jewelry and ornaments and distributed them to the poor, and confessed that she was a Christian. Her father was enraged; he threw her in prison then ordered to throw arrows at her. She delivered up her pure spirit in the hand of the Lord Christ and received the crown of martyrdom.

The Governor sent St. Jason to one of the islands to be tortured there. On his way the ship drowned in the sea but St. Jason was saved. He continued to teach and preach the name of Christ for many years until another Governor reigned. The new Governor brought him and all those who were with him, and tortured them. When the Governor saw that his torture did not harm their bodies, he and all those in his city also believed in the Lord Christ. The Saint baptized them, taught them the commandments of the Gospel, and built for them churches. God performed by his hands many miracles and signs. He departed in peace in a good old age.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-03.title: The Departure of St. Jason, One of the Seventy Disciples

09-03.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.), St. Otimus the priest was martyred. He was born in Fowwa, and because of his godliness and uprightness, he was ordained a priest for his hometown. He taught and confirmed the believers in the faith. When Emperor Diocletian incited the persecution against the Christians, the governor heard of him and he brought him. He suggested to him that he worship the idols; however, the Saint did not hearken to his orders. He tortured him much, but the Lord strengthened him. Finally, the governor ordered to burn him alive, and, thus, he received the crown of martyrdom.

His body was taken by a God fearing priest who shrouded the body and hid it in a place until the end of the era of persecution. Then they built a church after his name where God revealed many miracles.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-03.title: The Martyrdom of St. Otimus, the Priest

09-03.html:
On this day also of the year 1094 of the martyrs (1378 A.D.), Pope Gabriel IV, 86th Patriarch, departed. He was the abbot of the monastery of the holy Virgin Mary known as El-Muharraq monastery. He was a knowledgeable, ascetic and godly father. He was consecrated patriarch on the 11th of Tobe, year 1086 of the martyrs (1370 A.D.).

The place of his residence was in Haret Zowaila and he consecrated the holy Myron along with 10 bishops. He composed many melodies in Coptic and Greek in the Koiahk Psalmody.

He was a contemporary of El-Sultan Shabaan Ebn-Hassan and El-Sultan Ali Ebn-Shabaan El-Mansur. He sat on the apostolic throne for eight years, three months, and 22 days, and then departed in peace. He was buried beside St. Simeon the tanner in El-Habash monastery.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-03.title: The Departure of Pope Gabriel IV, the 86th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-04.html:
On this day of the year 221 of the martyrs (505 A.D.), Pope John I (Yoannis), 29th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. This Holy Father was born in Alexandria to Christian parents. He was inclined since his youth to the monastic life. He became a monk in the monastery of St. Macarius. When he was chosen patriarch, he refused, however, the bishops, priests, and lay leaders compelled him to go with them. He was consecrated on the 1st day of Paope of the year 213 of the martyrs (496 A.D.) After his enthronement, he gave special attention to teaching, exhorting and confirming the faithful in the Orthodox faith.

Emperor Zeno had died and the righteous Emperor Anastasius reigned after him. St. Severus of Antioch wrote to the emperor a letter in which he explained the principles of the Orthodox faith. Macedonius II Patriarch of Constantinople had severed the relationship with the Church of Alexandria and the Church of Antioch. He also affirmed the decisions of the Council of Chalcedon. A council was convened against him, in the capital city, by the order of the Emperor which deposed him from the patriarchal throne and exiled him. A godly man by the name of Timothy I was consecrated in his place. Once he was enthroned, he convened a council in which he refused the canons of the Council of Chalcedon and declared his union with the Churches of Alexandria and Antioch.

For this reason the hand of the patriarch was strengthened in spreading the Orthodox faith in all of Egypt. During the papacy of Pope Yoannis, the Church of Alexandria flourished for the people were secure and in peace. The Emperor was a peaceful man who sent to the wilderness of Shiheet what the fathers the monks needed. All the days of this pope were days of peace and tranquility except for the plague which spread in Alexandria that caused the deaths of many of his children. When he finished his good endeavor, he became ill for a short time, and then departed in peace, after he had been on the apostolic throne for eight years and seven months.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-04.title: The Departure of Pope John I (Yoannis), the 29th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-04.html:
On this day also of the year 882 of the martyrs (1166 A.D.), Pope Yoannis V, the 72nd Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. His name was John (Yoannis) Ebn Abe El-Fatah. He was enthroned on the second day of the Little Month, of the year 863 of the martyrs (1147 A.D.).

During his days the Copts were persecuted by the Muslim governors and Khalifas; many were martyred or imprisoned. They destroyed the churches and plundered their vessels and valuables. But when the political disturbances subsided, the Coptic layman el-Asa’ad Salib took charge of rebuilding the churches that were destroyed, renovated the ruined ones, and bought the needed altar utensils for them.

The patriarch was imprisoned during the days of El-Aadel Ebn El-Selar because he refused to ordain a metropolitan for Ethiopia instead of its metropolitan who was still alive. The metropolitan's name was Abba Michael El-Atfihi. The ruler also ordered the Christians in Egypt to put girdles or belts around their waists and not to wear the shawls that are worn over the head and shoulders. The pope was released two weeks later because of the death of El-Aadel.

Also during the days of this patriarch, the words "Life-giving" were added to the confession which became: “This is the Life-giving Flesh that your only-begotten Son, our Lord, God and Savior, Jesus Christ, took from our Lady...”

A famine, severe inflation and plague struck that the cattle, and the persecution of his people affected the health of the pope. He departed delivering his soul into the hands of the heavenly Father. The faithful buried him in the church of Abu Safain in Old Cairo after he had been on the apostolic throne for 18 years, eight months, and four days.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-04.title: The Departure of Pope Yoannis V, the 72nd Patriarch of Alexandria

09-05.html:
On this day, the great prophet Jeremiah, one of the Major Prophets, was martyred. He was the son of Hilkiah the priest and was born in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin which was nearby Jerusalem. Because of his kinship to a priestly family, he was well acquainted with the law of Moses and regularly attending the holy convocations and the feasts of the Lord.

The Lord had called him for the prophetic work in a vision about the time of the prophet-hood of Zephaniah the prophet. When Jeremiah objected because of his young age, the Lord put forth His hand and touched his mouth and said; “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth. See, I have this day set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out and to pull down, to destroy and to throw down, and to build and to plant.”

He started his prophetic work in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah, king of Judah, in the year 629 B.C. and prophesied eighteen years during his reign. He also prophesied during the three months in which Jehoahaz reigned, the eleven years reign of Jehoiakim, and the eleven years and five months reign of Zedekiah. He served the Lord for 41 years ended by the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 588 B.C., added to that the time he prophesied in Egypt.

He started his prophetic ministry in Anathoth and faced resistance from his tribe for this reason he cried to the Lord to bring His judgment upon them. Before long the resistance spread and became everywhere, so he cried again to the Lord to bring His judgment upon those who were resisting. In spite of this he remained faithful to his endeavor.

In the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim, he dictated his prophecy that he uttered in the previous twenty years to Baruch the scribe who transcribed it and read it in the Temple. When this scroll was read before the king, he tore it and threw it in the fire. Jeremiah wrote it once more.

When Jerusalem was under siege, the Jewish authorities considered the prophecies of Jeremiah pertaining to the besieging of Jerusalem by the Chaldeans and the exile of Judah. They were exacerbated from him and he was thrown into the dungeon. After many days King Zedekiah released him and asked him secretly; “Is there any word from the Lord?” And Jeremiah said, “You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon!” Then Zedekiah commanded that they should commit Jeremiah to the court of the prison and to treat him somewhat nicer. Nevertheless the princes cast him in the dungeon to die from hunger. An Ethiopian eunuch had compassion on Jeremiah so he asked for the permission of the king to lift him up from the dungeon. He allowed him and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken.

When the Chaldeans knew of his suffering, Nebuchadnezzar ordered to release him. Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard offered him to live in Babylon but he refused and chose the land of Judah to dwell among his brothers who remained after the fall of Jerusalem. Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam and dwelt with him. When Gedaliah was killed, Jeremiah urged the people not to escape to Egypt but they refused his advice moreover they forced him to go with them and there he uttered his last prophecies in Tahpanhes.

Jeremiah had a loving heart and had no aptitude for sin or the perishing of his people. His soul was bitter for he lived in a time marked by corruption of the people of Judah. That made him, with profound love, declaring the truth and admonishing the rulers, the kings of Judah, the priests, the false prophets and the people warning them with the judgments of God. He was continually weeping for his people, for this reason he was called “the weeping prophet.”

He appealed to the people to repent by declaring to them the mercies of God and his divine forgiveness. He also foretold of the end of exile after seventy years, the fall of the great city Babylon hence the empire loses its might. Finally he foretold the blessings that are kept for the people of God in the latter days in the kingdom of the Lord Christ.

Beside his prophetic book he also wrote the Lamentations in which he lamented, the falling of Jerusalem, its destruction and the severe suffering that befell those defended the city from hunger and the sword. He revealed in the Lamentation that the sin of people was the reason of the disaster.

This great prophet remained holding fast to his perfection, faithfulness to God, the zeal for his people, blamed them for their sins especially for worshipping the idols. He advised them to return to God however he was martyred in Egypt for the Jews stoned him to death.

The blessing of the prayers of this great prophet be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-05.title: The Martyrdom of Jeremiah the Prophet

09-06.html:
On this day of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Isaac El-Defrawi (of Tiphre), was martyred. Isaac was born in the city of Tiphre (Defra). When he was twenty-five years old the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a vision, while he was asleep in the field and told him; “Peace unto you O Isaac, the pious man of God, why are you asleep and the strife is going on.” Then the angel showed him a crown and his heart was inflamed with desire to receive the crown of martyrdom. In the next morning he went to his parents to bid them farewell to go to the city of Towa. They wept and forbade him from leaving. In the middle of the night the house lighted up with a brilliant light then the angel appeared and encouraged Isaac to go to fulfill the desire of his heart. Immediately he left his hometown and went to Towa.

He professed his faith before the Governor, shouting and saying: "I believe in the Lord Christ". The Governor placed him under guard until he had returned from the city of Nakyos.

It happened that when St. Isaac was guarded by the soldier, a blind man asked him for a charity. The saint entreated God for his sake and his eyes were opened and the soldier immediately believed. When the Governor returned, the soldier confessed his faith before him. The governor ordered to behead him thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The Governor became angry at St. Isaac, and tormented him severely, then sent him to the governor of el-Bahnasa. He was bound on the boat so he asked one of the sailors who was blind in one eye to bring him a little of water. He gave him water to drink however the cup fell from him. A drop of the water fell on the sailor’s eye and the man received the sight in his blind eye immediately.

When the Saint met the governor of El-Bahnasa, he tried to befriend him to persuade him to forsake his faith however when he failed, the Governor tortured him severely, but the Lord comforted and healed him. Arianus the governor of Ansena was present, the governor of el-Bahnasa informed him about the account of St.Isaac el-Defrawi. Arianus took the saint with him to Ansena where he tormented him severely and when he became weary of torturing him he sent him to Towa where he was beheaded, thus he received the crown of martyrdom. Some of the faithful took his body and carried it to his town Defra and buried him there. Later on a church was built after his name which was consecrated on the 6th of Tobe. After a while his body was relocated to Sonbat.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-06.title: The Martyrdom of St. Isaac of Tiphre (El-Defrawi)

09-06.html:
On this day also of the year 19 of the martyrs (303 A.D.) mother Dolagy and her four children, Soris, Horman, Abanoufa and Shentas, were martyred. When Arianus, governor of Ansena, arrived to Esna, these four brothers met him when they were guiding their animals carrying watermelons. One of the governor’s soldiers asked them about their belief. They professed their faith in the Lord Christ so they seized them.

When their mother knew, she went in haste to encourage and strengthen their faith. The governor ordered to also imprison her. During the night the holy Virgin St. Mary appeared to her and told her that the Lord Christ had prepared for her and her children the crowns.

The next morning the governor summoned them and ordered them to raise incense before the idols however they refused and declared their Christianity. The governor ordered to slay them so the mother came forward and offered them one after the other to be assured of their steadfastness in their faith. The governor, for his cruelty, he ordered to slay them on her knees. Then they beheaded mother Dolagy after them and they all received the crowns of martyrdom.

The believers took their bodies and buried them in their house which became later on a church after their names. A Church after their names is presently located in the city of Esna.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-06.title: The Martyrdom of Mother Dolagy and Her Four Children

09-06.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) the Holy Father Anba Babnuda (Paphnute) who was from El-Bandarah, was martyred. He was of a noble descent and lived a life of worship, godliness and fear of God. He worked in farming.

The angel of God appeared to him and exhorted him to seek the crown of martyrdom. He rejoiced for the invocation and distributed all his money to the poor. He went to Alexandria and confessed before its governor his faith in the Lord Christ. The governor tormented him severely however the angel of the Lord healed him.

In prison he healed the eyes of the son of the jailer who believed in the Lord Christ. He confessed his faith before the governor who ordered to behead him and his entire household.

When the governor took St. Babnuda to raise incense for the idol, the saint prayed to God and the devil inside the idol spoke, and immediately all the idols fell. When all those who were present saw that, they confessed the Lord Christ and were martyred. Then the governor ordered to imprison the saint without food or drink to die. Fifteen days later they took him out of prison and brought him before the governor and his face was shining. He tried to persuade him to change his resolve and to raise incense before the idol. When he refused they hung him from his feet and tied a heavy stone to his neck. Archangel Michael came down and saved him.

Among the crowd was a woman carrying a child afflicted with smallpox and blindness. She took from the blood of the saint and anointed his eyes and body and he was immediately healed. She glorified God and believed in the Lord Christ. When the governor knew that he ordered her beheaded along with her son thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

When the governor saw the old age of the saint he told him; “You are a wise old man and you can be an advisor for Emperor Diocletian.” The saint replied; “I am a soldier of the true king Jesus Christ.” The governor ordered to bind him and be thrown to the lions however they kneeled before him. The governor thought that it was a work of sorcery and told the saint; “O you crafty magician you have led the people astray with your God Jesus Christ.” The saint answered him saying; “You would be from now on mute until you confess the Lord Christ.” When he could not talk he pointed with his hand his confession and immediately his tongue was loosened. He stood and kissed the head of the saint and told him; “You are a godly, honorable old man, now let us eat and drink so your soul would be refreshed that you may offer the incense to the gods. When he refused to go with him to his house, the governor ordered to strike his body with iron pins then to throw him in prison. In prison he met St. Thomas of Shandalat and St. Shinosy of Balkeem. In the next morning they placed him in a cauldron full of oil, sulfur and pitch, then poured vinegar and lime down his throat and nose, finally they lit fire under him. The saint endured these tortures and the Archangel Michael came down and healed him.

Arianus, the governor of Ansena, was present and marveled at what he saw. In the next day he ordered the saint to raise incense to the idols but he refused and confessed the Lord Christ before him. Arianus was furious and ordered to hang him from a tree and to tie a heavy stone to his feet. The angel of the Lord appeared and saved him. Arianus was exasperated and threw him in prison. When he became weary of torturing him he ordered him beheaded thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The believers took his body, shrouded it and sent it to his hometown. When he arrived the people received him with great veneration and placed the body in the church. Many signs and wonders were manifested from his body. Later on the body was relocated to the city of el-kershyah then to Sonbat.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-06.title: The Martyrdom of Anba Paphnute of El-Bandarah

09-06.html:
On this day also of the year 109 of the martyrs (393 A.D.) the blessed father St. Macarius of Alexandria departed. He was one of the three saints Abba Macarii. He was born in Alexandria in the year 296 A.D. to a poor family. In the beginning he worked as a baker made sweets and cakes and sold them. He received the sacrament of holy baptism when he was thirty years old and was filled with the grace of God. He heard the accounts of the ascetics and the monks. He visited St. Anthony the father of all monks in the year 335 A.D. On his way back he went to the wilderness of Nitria and he was about 38 years old. This region was filled with monastic cells which were established about the year 315 A.D. by St. Amoun.

He became a disciple of St. Amoun for two years until his departure in the year 337 A.D. then to his successor St. Pamo (Pambo) who presided over the monastery in the year 340 A.D.

When the ascetic life of St. Macarius was well rooted and grew in his spiritual strife he went to the Pachomian monastery at Tabennesi in disguise. When the abbot of the monastery saw that he was an old man, he prevented him for his inability to endure the harsh life. After much insistence the abbot accepted him and that was during the holy forty days of Lent. He fasted during the week and ate a few cabbage leaves on Sunday beside his vigils and working with his hands. All that led to severe weakness and his body became severely emaciated. The monks complained to St. Pachomius, Father of the Koinonia, saying; “Cast out this man from here for he is not human.” However St. Pachom recognized him by divine guidance.

When his secret was revealed, he went and lived in seclusion in the region of the cells (Cellia) which is about 20 kilometers from Nitria. St. Isidore was the priest of Cellia; however he went to Shiheet to assist St. Macarius the great (the Egyptian). In the year 355 A.D. St. Macarius was ordained a priest and became the abbot of Cellia instead of St. Isidore. After the departure of St. Pamo in the year 373 A.D. St. Macarius of Alexandria also presided over the area of Nitria. The two areas, Nitria and Cellia, became close to each other because the number of monks dwelt in them had greatly increased. He remained as such until his departure in the year 393 A.D.

He was also exiled along with St. Macarius the great to the island of Philae. The Arian Emperor Valens had exiled them to this island.

God had granted this saint the gift of performing miracles. He was a gentle and simple joyful man. When he finished his good endeavor and well fought spiritual strife, departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-06.title: The Departure of St. Macarius of Alexandria

09-06.html:
On this day of the year 1734 for the martyrs, corresponding to May 14, 2018 AD, a private plane carrying twenty coffins landed at Cairo International Airport containing the relics of the twenty Coptic martyrs who were martyred in Libya.

His Holiness Pope Tawadros II, 118th Pope received them with a number of venerable bishops, priests, deacons and archons, while praying in the joyful tune.

Then twenty ambulances took them to the Church of the Martyrs in the village of Al-Awar, Samalut Center - Minya Governorate. The ambulances arrived the next morning, and there the coffins were placed at the bottom of the church with their belongings.

As for the bodies, they were buried together under the altar at the bottom of the church, under the supervision and presence of Anba Paphnutius, Metropolitan of Samalout, and in the presence of the governor of Minya and the director of security.

These martyrs were from some villages in Minya and went to Libya to work there, and when the terrorist organization ISIS increased and took control of some areas of the country, some Christians who were working there began to be arrested and killed. Among them, these twenty martyrs were arrested in two batches, the first batch on December 30, 2014, they arrested 7 Egyptians in the Libyan city of Sirte, and the second batch on January 3, 2015, they arrested 13 Egyptians and one from Ghana.

In the same city of Sirte, they continued to torment them severely for more than a month in order to deny their faith in Christ, but they persistently refused and adhered to their faith and used to pray and repeat the “Lord Have Mercy” or “Kyrie Layson” prayer frequently. Eyewitnesses said that the earth was shaking under them and that they saw some of the saints around them.

On February 5, 2015, ISIS soldiers took them to the Mediterranean coast outside the city of Sirte and slaughtered them like sheep without mercy and with extreme brutality, and so they obtained the crowns of martyrdom.

ISIS terrorists buried the bodies of the martyrs in a public grave outside the city of Sirte, and the bodies remained buried in that unknown place for more than three years, until someone who attended the massacre and saw the burial place informed the authorities. The Libyan authorities, in cooperation with the Egyptian authorities, took them out and returned them to Egypt with all honor and reverence.

May the blessing of these honorable martyrs be with us all, and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-06.title: The Arrival of the Relics of the Coptic Martyrs of Libya

09-07.html:
On this day of the year 89 of the martyrs (373 A.D.) the great saint Pope Athanasius, the apostolic, the 20th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in Alexandria about the year 297 A.D. He longed to be Christian after he had been touched by the morality of the Christians.

Pope Alexandros baptized him and shortly after he ordained him deacon and took him as his disciple. He was also discipled as a monk by St. Anthony the father of all monks. He manifested his early distinction in his two books; “Against the Heathen” (Contra Gentes) and “The Incarnation of the word of God”.

Deacon Athanasius attended the council of Nicaea along with Pope Alexandros in the year 325 A.D. where he vanquished Arius the heretic. On the 8th of Pashons year 44 of the martyrs (328 A.D.) he was consecrated patriarch after the departure of his teacher Pope Alexandros which he commanded before his departure. Athanasius was a thirty years old young man. He guided the church for seven years in a tranquil atmosphere. During this time he ordained for Ethiopia its first bishop whose name was Frumentius “Anba Salama" bishop for Aksum (Axum) in Ethiopia about the year 330 A.D. Pope Athanasius also went on a pastoral visit to Upper Egypt during which he met St. Pachom father of the Koinonia who ran away until he was assured that he would not be ordained a priest.

St. Athanasius was exiled away from his Chair five times:

The First Exile:

The hardships started to pursue Pope Athanasius after Emperor Constantine issued his orders to accept Arius in the fellowship of the church. Arius had pretended that he had repented and wrote the creed of his faith in a devious way. Nevertheless, Pope Athanasius refused to accept him so the Emperor exiled him.

It is worthy to note that Eusebius of Nicomedia (An Arian bishop) had exerted great efforts to force the return of Arius to the fellowship of the church. That disturbed St. Alexandros, Patriarch of Constantinople, for they forced him to accept Arius. Arius died a horrible death for he died on his way to the church in a public washroom, where his bowels poured out of his body.

Nearly a year later Constantine commended, while he was on his death bed, the return of Athanasius to Alexandria. The Pope returned to his flock with great veneration.

The Second Exile:

The attacks of the enemies of Athanasius did not quiet down what necessitated St. Anthony to go down to Alexandria to support, his disciple, the suffering Pope.

In the year 338 A.D. Emperor Constantius ordered to convene a council in Antioch in which they issued a decree to depose Athanasius. The Emperor also appointed instead Gawargios of Antioch a bishop and ruler for Alexandria. St. Anthony sent letters to the alien bishop and some of his officers to reprove them for their actions. St. Pachom also sent two of his excellent monks who were Zakaros and Tadros to support the believers in Alexandria during the absence of the Pope.

In the year 339 A.D. Athanasius travelled to his friend Julius, Bishop of Rome. Since that time monasticism spread to the west as a result of the book written by Pope Athanasius about the life of St. Anthony. In the year 342 A.D. the Pope met with the Emperor of the West Constance in Milan and convinced him of assembling a council. He agreed with the Emperor of the East to convene the council in Serdica in the year 343 A.D.

The Arian bishops came from the East and refused to attend the council because of the participation of Athanasius and his supporters in it. When the council convened, it excommunicated eleven Arian bishops which provoked the Arians. They tried to hinder the return of Athanasius to Alexandria. However the Emperor ordered the return of all who were in exile. He also sent three letters to Athanasius revealed in them his desire to see him. Later on he met the Emperor before his return to Alexandria in the year 346 A.D. and his flock received him with great joy.

The Third Exile:

The Arians did not like the return of Athanasius to Alexandria, and waited impatiently until the murder of Emperor Constans, Pope Athanasius friend. The Arians accused Athanasius of having a secret relation with the murderer. After Constantius, Emperor of the East and West, had got rid of the murderer, he devoted himself to resist the Pope for he hated him. He forced the bishops of the East and West to assemble two councils the first in Arles in France in the year 353 A.D. and the second in Milan in the year 355 A.D. to depose the Pope and exile him.

In the year 356 A.D. the soldiers attacked the church of St. Mary which was built by Pope Theonas (16th Patriarch) while Pope Athanasius was praying. The soldiers rushed inside the church to arrest him, but God blinded them from recognizing him and he remained in the church until every person departed the church in peace. The priests asked him to escape and he was in his free will exile moving from monastery to monastery. His heart was inflamed with his love for God and his flock, shepherding his children through his profound writings. He wrote the biography of St. Antonius (Vita Antoni), sent letters to the bishops of Egypt, Libya and to the Egyptian monks, four apologetic articles against the Arians, five theological letters to Serapion, bishop of Thmuis, concerning the Holy Spirit and a book about the councils.

In the year 362 A.D. the Pope returned after the death of Constantius.

The Fourth Exile:

After the death of Constantius, Julian succeeded him. Athanasius assembled a council called “the council of the saints and confessors.” Emperor Julian felt the threat of Athanasius against pagan worship. He sent a letter to the governor of Alexandria to expel Athanasius. The Pope was forced to hide in the tomb of his father for six months. When the Emperor tightened the grip around the governor to seize him, Athanasius was forced to leave Alexandria and took a boat to Upper Egypt. The Governor followed him in another boat, and when he caught up with the boat of Athanasius, he asked about the where-about of the Pope. Athanasius told them he was not too far away from you. The Governor went on his way in hurry to Upper Egypt. Athanasius returned and moved among the monasteries until he settled in Akhmim.

The period of the fourth exile had ended by Julian death for he was killed in his war against the Persians. Jovian succeeded him and he sent a letter to Athanasius asking him to return to his church. The Pope returned to Alexandria and assembled a council and wrote a letter which included the Nicene Creed of Faith. Then he went to meet the Emperor who received him with a warm welcome and returned him to Alexandria in the year 364 A.D.

The Fifth Exile:

After the death of Jovian, Valentinian reigned in the West and appointed his brother Valens Emperor for the East and he was Arian. Valens ordered the banishment of all the bishops who were exiled before during the reign of Julian to the places of their previous exile. Athanasius was forced to leave Alexandria to the fifth exile. He hid in a rural house in the year 365 A.D. He spent nine months in hiding and returned at the age of seventy to his throne because of the pressure of his people against the rulers. In the year 366 A.D. he returned to Alexandria among the joy and jubilation of his flock.

He returned to shepherd his flock with a fiery spirit and zeal especially to purge the faith of the church from any Arian thought. In the year 369 A.D. he assembled a council in Alexandria was attended by ninety bishops to confirm the Orthodox Faith. The Pope continued to be active spiritually and theologically until he reached the age of seventy six years old to hand to the generations the custody of the Orthodox faith without any deviation.

He departed in peace after he had been on the Apostolic Throne for forty five years.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-07.title: The Departure of St. Athanasius the Apostolic the 20th Pope of Alexandria

09-08.html:
On this day is the commemoration of the Ascension of Our Lord Jesus Christ to heaven. We have to put in our account that the Resurrection was on the 29th day of Paremhotep.

May His holy blessing be with us all. Amen
09-08.title: The Commemoration of the Ascension of Our Lord Jesus Christ to Heaven

09-08.html:
On this day also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) St. John of Senhout was martyred. He was born in Senhout, his father's name was Macarius and his mother's name was Anna.

It came to pass, when he was tending his father’s sheep, the angel of the Lord appeared to him, showed him a crown of light and said to him: "Why are you sitting here and the strife is at hand, now rise up and go to the city of Attrib and strive for the Name of the Lord Christ"; then the angel gave him the salutation of peace and departed from him.

He bade farewell to his parents, went to the Governor, and confessed the Lord Christ before him. The Governor handed him to one of the soldiers to befriend him and treat him kindly that he might change his counsel. The Saint performed several miracles before the soldier that made him believe in the Lord Christ and received the crown of martyrdom by the hands of the Governor.

The Governor became angry and tormented the Saint with every kind of torture however the Lord comforted and strengthened him. Then he sent the Saint to Ansena, where he was tortured again and finally he was beheaded with the sword.

St. Julius of Aqfahs (el-Akfehasi) shrouded his body, and sent it to his home-town Senhout. The people received him with hymns and praises, and placed him in the church. The body of the Saint now is located in Shoubra El-Khema in Egypt.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-08.title: The Martyrdom of St. John of Senhout

09-08.html:
On this day also of the year 296 of the martyrs (580 A.D.) the Holy Father Anba Daniel the Hegumen of the wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis), departed. He was born about the year 485 A.D. and went to Shiheet in his youth. He ate daily at sunset and worked in making baskets.

Because of the successive raids of the barbarians and the thieves on the wilderness, the monks abandoned it fleeing from the danger. Abba Daniel was captured by the Berbers three times. After a period of worship and asceticism the Pope ordained him Hegumen for the wilderness.

One day, the Saint saw a person whose name was Olagi (Eulogius), who worked as a stone cutter and from what he earned he fed the poor and housed the sojourners. When Abba Daniel saw the excellence of his deeds, he asked God to give him more money to abound his deeds of mercy. God answered his prayer and when he had much money he went to Constantinople. Eulogius sought a high ranking position and notability and forsook the deeds of mercy.

Abba Daniel saw in a vision as if the Lord Christ is sitting judging among the people and demanded from him the lost soul of Olagi. He entreated God to save Olagi and bring him back to his virtuous life. The angel of the Lord appeared to him and rebuked him for rejecting God's judgment of His creation. Eulogius participated in an upheaval against Emperor Justinian and Olagi was saved miraculously and left behind all his wealth and returned back to his former state.

As of Anba Daniel, when the envoy arrived with the Tome of Leo, which was affirmed by the council of Chalcedon, to the wilderness of Shiheet, to be signed and approved by the monks, Anba Daniel and the monks refused to sign it. Accordingly the soldiers very roughly handled them with many beatings. Daniel found a refuge at Tambok, a little village of the district of Shoubra-Kheet, el-Beheira governorate. He dwelt there until the death of Justinian in the year 565 A.D. when he returned to Shiheet. In the year 577 A.D. was the fourth raid of the Berbers so he returned to Tambok where he departed to the Lord. He was more than ninety five years old.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-08.title: The Departure of St. Daniel the Hegumen of the Wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis)

09-09.html:
On this day of the year 327 A.D., St. Helena, the Empress, departed. She was born in the city of el-Raha (Urfa-Edessa) to Christian parents about the year 247 A.D. They brought her up in a Christian manner and she was beautiful and gentle. When Emperor Constantius the First, Emperor of Byzantium, came to the city of el-Raha, he sought her out and married her. She gave birth to Constantine and she raised him up well, and taught him philosophy, wisdom and knighthood. After the death of his father he became the emperor of the East and his capital city was Constantinople.

One day he saw a vision in the middle of the day, a cross of light and written under it; “With this sign you shall conquer.” He placed the sign of the cross on his flag and on all his armaments. He was victorious in the war and he also became the emperor of the West.

Queen Helena, when she was about seventy years old, saw in a vision as someone telling her; "Go to Jerusalem and search for the Cross of the Savior.” When she told her son, he sent her with an entourage of soldiers to Jerusalem. She met there St. Macarius bishop of Jerusalem and inquired from him about the place where the cross was buried. St. Helena asked the Jews about the whereabouts of the cross they told her about an old Jew who informed her about a hill on the top of which a pagan temple of Venus was built. Emperor Hadrian built it in the year 135 A.D. to ensure the complete disappearance of the cross.

Queen Helena ordered the demolition of the temple and the removal of the pile of dirt. She found three crosses and they confirmed the cross of the Lord when they placed it on a dead person who arose immediately. They also found what was written by Pontius Pilate on the top of the cross: "This is Jesus, king of the Jews."

She gave the needed money to Anba Macarius to build the church of the Resurrection on the site of the holy sepulcher, another church above the manger of Bethlehem and a third church on the place of ascension on Mount Olive.

On her return she took a nail from the cross to her son which he placed on the royal helmet. She also sent a piece of the honorable Cross to the royal palace in Constantinople. The rest of the cross was placed in a case made of gold and placed it in the church of Resurrection under the care of the bishop Macarius.

St. Helena led a righteous life, built many churches and monasteries and she endowed much funds for their care and for the poor. She departed in peace at age of eighty years old.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-09.title: The Departure of St. Helena, the Queen

09-09.html:
On this day also of the year 1168 of the martyrs (1452 A.D.) Pope Yoannis XI, 89th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. His name was Abouna al-Asa’ad Abu el-Farag, the priest of the church of the martyr Mercurius Abu Safain in Old Cairo.

He was consecrated a patriarch on the 16th day of Pashons, year 1143 of the martyrs (1427 A.D.). His residence was in the patriarchal cell in Haret Zowaila. He was contemporary to the rulers El-Ashraf, El-Aziz, El-Zaher, and El-Mansour. In the beginning of his papacy, an earthquake took place, shortage of the water of the Nile, severe inflation that went on for two years and the spread of the Plague.

He encountered many hardships that required the intervention of the king of Ethiopia who threatened the Egyptian government to cut the flow of the Nile because of the persecution of the Copts. The Pope was beaten, imprisoned and they confiscated his funds. The Patriarch was forbidden from communicating with the king of Ethiopia without the permission and knowledge of the rulers of the government. He was also not allowed to ordain metropolitans or bishops for Ethiopia without permission from el-Sultan. When the water of the Nile came short, the prices increased and was shortage of bread, the Copts prayed for consecutive days and the water level was risen up in the month of Thoout.

During his days were many prominent fathers guarded and struggled for the sake of faith and strengthened the resolve of the Christians. Among them were Anba Koriakos bishop of el-Bahnasa, Anba Ghobrial bishop of Assuit and Tag el-Dein Ebn Nasr-Allah the scribe of prince Barsabay.

After all these hardships the pope departed and was buried in El-Khandaq monastery. He remained on the apostolic throne for 24 years, 11 months and 23 days.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-09.title: The Departure of Pope Yoannis XI, 89th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-09.html:
On this day also of the year 1319 of the martyrs (1603 A.D.) Pope Gabriel VIII, 97th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in the city of Meer, and became a monk by the name of Shenouda in the monastery of Anba Pishoy. He was consecrated Patriarch on the 16th day of Paone, year 1302 of the martyrs (1586 A.D.) and he resided in Haret Zowaila.

Disturbances took place during his time for the soldiers clashed with the people for the taxes had no fixed system and the Mamlukes levied the taxes as they wished. Injustice, famine, inflation and plague spread all over the land. Then a severe earthquake shook the land destroying many buildings.

During his days also Pope of Rome tried again to force the Copts to confess his supremacy over the Coptic Church. Pope Gabriel and the Coptic people became more enthusiastic to keep the independence of their church. That way the negotiation of the Roman delegates failed.

They went to Ethiopia; however Pope Gabriel sent a letter to the king and the Ethiopian clergy warning them from abandoning the Orthodox faith. Nevertheless, the Ethiopian king and some men of his government followed the pope of Rome. When Anba Khristozoulos, bishop of Ethiopia, failed to convince the king, he declared his excommunication. The people rose up against the king and slew him.

Later on pope Gabriel departed in the monastery of the Virgin Mary known as El-Syrian and was buried there, after he had been on the apostolic throne for fifteen years, ten months, and twenty-four days.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-09.title: The Departure of Pope Gabriel VIII, 97th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-10.html:
On this day the church commemorates the departure of the three holy young men: Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael. They were of the tribe of Judah and were exiled by Nebuchadnezzar to Babylon and he chose them along with Daniel to serve in his palace. He gave them Chaldean names; Daniel the name Belteshazzar, to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abed-Nego.

These young men purposed in their heart that they would not defile themselves with the portion of the king's delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank. They asked the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had set over them: "Please test your servants for ten days, and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink. Then let our countenances be examined before you, and the countenances of the young men who eat the portion of the king's delicacies; and as you see fit, so deal with your servants." And at the end of ten days their countenance appeared better than all the young men who ate the portion of the king's delicacies. As for these four young men, God gave them knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom. The King appointed them governors on all the provinces of Babylon. (Daniel 1:8-20)

When they did not worship the image of gold, the king brought them and asked them about that and they confessed that they only worship the true God. He commanded them to be cast in a burning fiery furnace. The Lord came down by Himself, protected them and made the fire as cool dew although it burnt the men that threw them in the fiery furnace. When the king saw that, he praised and blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-Nego and promoted them in the province of Babylon.

When they completed their strife while they were praying, and kneeling down in their home, they gave up their spirits in the hand of the Lord. A great earthquake took place in the city. The king was terrified, and was told that the three Hebrew young men had died. The king grieved and ordered to make for them three beds made of ebony, and their bodies be wrapped in apparels made of silk. He also ordered a bed made of gold for himself, so that when he died, they would place him on it among them.

It happened during the days of Pope Theophilus, 23rd Patriarch of Alexandria; he built a church after their names and wanted to relocate their bodies to it. He delegated St. John Colobos (the short) and sent him to Babylon. When he arrived to where the bodies were, he heard a voice from them saying: "The Lord has ordained that our bodies would remain in this place till the day of Resurrection, but because of your labor of love, when you return, say to the Patriarch to fill the oil lamps with oil on the night of the consecration of the church, and the power of God will be revealed. For we will come and light them and attend the consecration prayer." Indeed at the beginning of the consecration prayer a great light shone in the church and all the oil lamps (Kandeels) lighted up and the smell of perfumed incense spread. Pope Theophilus saw the three young men walking along with him during the prayers.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-10.title: The Departure of the Three Holy Young Men Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael

09-11.html:
On this day of the year 570 of the martyrs (1034 A.D.) St. Paphnute, the bishop, departed. He became a monk in the monastery of St. Macarius. He exerted himself in asceticism and worship. He learned in the wilderness how to read and write. He excelled in studying the Holy Scriptures, the canons of the church and the church fathers. He was ordained a priest, and after staying in the wilderness for thirty five years, his virtues became well known. Pope Philotheos I, 63rd Patriarch of Alexandria, ordained him bishop.

He did not change his apparel which was made of goat’s hair except on the day of celebrating the Divine Liturgy then he put it on again. Because of his austere asceticism his body wasted away and became ill. He asked God in his prayer saying: "O My Lord Jesus Christ, do not take away Your blessings from me because of the episcopate." The angel of the Lord appeared and told him: "You know when you were in the wilderness, there was no one to take care of you in your sickness and you could not find medications but God supported, sustained you, and kept sickness away from you. However, you are now in the world, and there are many who can take care of you and treat you in your sickness."

This father was a bishop for thirty two years. When the day of his departure drew near, he called the priests and the deacons, handed to them the sacred properties of the church and told them; “I have never kept for myself even one dinar.” He blessed them, and then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-11.title: The Departure of St. Paphnotius (St. Paphnute), the Bishop

09-11.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Theoclia, the wife of St. Justus, son of emperor Numerianus, was martyred. After Emperor Diocletian had sent her, her husband and her son Abali to the Governor of Alexandria, Armanius, he tried to befriend and treat them kindly. When he failed, he separated them. He sent St. Justus to Ansena (Antinoe) where he received the crown of martyrdom. He sent Abali, his son, to Basta (nearby Zagazig, Sharqia) where he was martyred.

As of St. Theoclia, he sent her to the governor of Sa El-Hagar, Sharqia. When the Governor saw her, he was astonished to know that she was from a royal family and she could be a queen in spite of that she came with her complete own free will to endure the tortures. He at first tried to gently treat her but she told him: "What could you give me? I have left my kingdom, accepted the separation from my husband and my son for the sake of the Lord Christ." He ordered her beaten until her flesh was torn then cast her in prison. The angel of the Lord appeared to her, healed, comforted and strengthened her. Because of her, many of the prisoners who witnessed that believed in the Lord Christ, were martyred and received the crowns of martyrdom. Accordingly the Governor ordered to behead her thus she received the crown of martyrdom. Some of the believers came, paid the soldiers, took her body, shrouded and placed it in a coffin until the end of the days of persecution.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen
09-11.title: The Martyrdom of St. Theoclia, the wife of St. Justus

09-12.html:
On this day of each Coptic month the church celebrates a commemoration of the honorable Archangel Michael the head of the heavenly hosts and the intercessor of mankind.

His intercession be with us all. Amen.
09-12.title: The Commemoration of the Honorable Archangel Michael

09-12.html:
On this day also of the year 153 of the martyrs (437 A.D.) during the reign of Emperor Theodosius II (the Less) was the relocation of the relics of St. John Chrysostom (Golden Mouthed) took place from the city of Comana in Pontus, where he departed in exile to the city of Constantinople about thirty years after his departure.

When they arrived with the pure body to Constantinople, multitudes came out to receive their shepherd who was martyred without bloodshed, sacrificing his life for them. They celebrated him in a splendid celebration and laid him in the church of the holy Apostles. The Emperor knelt down before him with a contrite heart and tears flowing from his eyes asking for the forgiveness for himself and for his parents, Arcadius and Eudoxia.

The blessing of the prayers of St. John Chrysostom be with us all. Amen.
09-12.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the relics of St. John Chrysostom

09-12.html:
On this day also of the year 67 of the martyrs (351 A.D.) during the reign of Emperor Constantius, the son of Emperor Constantine the great, the sign of the honorable Cross appeared above Golgotha.

That was also during the time of St. Kyrillos (Cyril) bishop of Jerusalem who wrote saying; “During the holy days of the feast of Pentecost about the third hour of the day appeared in the sky the sign of the cross above Golgotha extended from the area above Jerusalem, from Golgotha to the mount of Olive. All those who were in Jerusalem saw it clearly. It did not disappear speedily as to be expected as a vision but remained seen to the naked eyes for many hours. It was shining with light more brilliant than that of the Sun. All the people of the city rushed outside to witness the sign and were astonished and overwhelmed but with joy of seeing this heavenly apparition. They all praised and glorified our Lord Jesus Christ.”

The blessing of the honorable Cross be with us all. Amen.
09-12.title: The Commemoration of the Appearance of a Cross of light above Golgotha

09-12.html:
On this day also of the year 1485 of the martyrs (1769 A.D.), Pope Mark VII, 106th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in the city of Klosna, by the name of Simeon, and he became a monk in the monastery of the saint Abba Paul. Pope Yoannis XVII, 105th Patriarch, ordained him a priest. After the departure of Pope Yoannis (John) he was chosen for the patriarchate for he was distinguished by compassion, pleasant voice, eloquence and wisdom. He was consecrated Patriarch on the 24th day of Pashons, year 1461 of the martyrs (1745 A.D.) which is the feast of the entry of the Lord Christ to Egypt.

After two years of his enthronement, there was a mutiny among the soldiers. Many of the Mamluk princes were killed and some escaped to Upper Egypt until the mutiny had died down. The Pope suffered a great deal in these days, from inside the church and from outside. God removed these tribulations after it had lingered for a time. This pope ordained Abba Peter, a Metropolitan for Akhmim, Girga and Upper Egypt and he also ordained Abba Yousab a Metropolitan for Ethiopia.

He remained on the apostolic throne for 23 years, 11 months and 8 days during which he suffered many hardships then departed in peace. He was in the monastery of the virgin, known as Adawyya, region of El-Maadi nearby Cairo. Before the departure of this Holy Father, he saw St. Anthony and Abba Paul present at the time of delivering his pure spirit. The church was celebrating the feast of St. Demiana, the commemoration of Archangel Michael, and St. John Chrysostom.

After his repose, they relocated his body in a boat to the monastery of St. George, in Old Cairo, and placed it in the convent under the shrine of the martyr and spent all night praying. The next morning they carried him in a procession headed by Anba Peter, Metropolitan of Upper Egypt, some bishops and priests to the church of St. Mercurius (Abu Safain), where they prayed over him and buried him in the tomb of the Patriarchs.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-12.title: The Departure of Pope Mark VII, 106th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-12.html:
On this day also, of the year 1519 of the martyrs (1803 A.D.) was the martyrdom of Master (Moallem) Malati Yousef. He worked as a scribe for Ayyub Beck El-Defterdar, one of the Mamlukes of Mohammed Beck Abu El-Dahab.

When the French occupied Egypt, they established an administrative office to look after the national affairs, and appointed Moallem Malati president with the consent of the Muslim and Christian members, for what this great man was distinguished with integrity, experience, patriotism and great managerial skills. After the French had left Egypt and the coming of the Turks it was advocated that no one to oppose the Christian notables specially el-Moallem Girgis El-Gohari, el-Moallem Wasef, and el-Moallem Malati. When disorder spread in the land and for the lack of public safety, in the days of Taher Pasha, the ruler of Egypt, they arrested Moallem Malati, and beheaded him at the gate of Haret Zowaila in Cairo, thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-12.title: The Martyrdom of Master (Moallem) Malati

09-12.html:
Today also of the year 43 of the martyrs (327 A.D.) was the consecration of the church of the martyr St. Demiana in el-Borolus.

St. Helena desired to receive the blessing from the body of the martyr St. Demiana after she heard the account of her martyrdom. When she arrived she found the bodies unharmed. After receiving the blessing she wrapped the bodies with expensive shrouds. She built a tomb (Cellar) underground where she placed the bodies. Then she built on the top of it a beautiful church with one dome. The church was consecrated by Pope Alexandros, 19th Patriarch of Alexandria, on the 12th day of Pashons. He also ordained a saintly bishop, priests, and deacons instead of those who were martyred during the time of Emperor Diocletian.

In the sixth century, Anba Youhanna (John), bishop of el-Borolus, renovated the church. That was during the papacy of Pope Demian, 35th Patriarch (year 569 – 605 A.D.). The church had many antiquated manuscripts among them was the biography of the martyr St. Demiana written by the hand of one of the disciples of St. Julius of Aqfahs, the writer of the biographies of the martyrs.

In the eighth century the church was completely ruined during the reign of Hassan Ibn Atahia, king of Egypt. He was just, loved the churches, and treated the bishops and the monks with great respect. He also loved Pope Khail I, 46th Patriarch of Alexandria (743 - 767 A.D.) During that time, the water of the Mediterranean Sea flooded the Delta because of the deterioration of the barrier, which held back the sea water. The Holy Father Pope Khail prayed in the presence of the King. God sent great wind which caused great quantities of sand to form a great barrier which was stronger than the original one. After that the Pope asked to build a church instead of the church that was ruined. When the church was completed, he consecrated it on the 12th day of the month of Pashons the same date for the consecration of the first church.

The blessing of the prayers of St. Demiana be with us all and Glory be to our God forever. Amen
09-12.title: The Commemoration of the Consecration of the church of St. Demiana

09-13.html:
On this day, in the year 163 of the martyrs (447 A.D.), the Holy Father St. Arsenius—tutor of the imperial children—departed in peace. He was born in Rome in 350 A.D. to wealthy and devout parents, who raised him in the teachings of the Church. He was ordained a deacon and mastered both Greek and Latin, excelling in them. His reputation for virtue and learning reached Emperor Theodosius the Great, who summoned Arsenius to instruct his two sons, Honorius and Arcadius. The young princes loved and respected him greatly.

Yet St. Arsenius was continually mindful of the vanity of the world. He often prayed, “Lord, guide me in the way of salvation.” One day he heard a divine voice saying, “Flee from people, and you shall be saved.” Obedient to this call, he took his sister to Constantinople and entrusted her to a convent of one hundred and twenty nuns. He then departed for Alexandria and from there journeyed to the wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis). He became first a disciple of St. John (Yehness) Colobos (The Short), and later of St. Isaiah the Elder (Al-Eskeety). He strove with great diligence in asceticism, fasting, prayer, and long night vigils. After three years, he again heard a voice saying, “Keep your serenity, withdraw from people, and be silent, and you will be saved.” He then secluded himself in a cave away from the monastery.

Once, seeking counsel about his thoughts, he spoke with one of the elders. A fellow monk overheard and asked him, “Does Arsenius—learned in Greek and Roman culture—seek advice from this uneducated Egyptian?” Arsenius replied, “In Greek and Roman knowledge I am well trained, but in the alphabet, in which this simple monk excels, I have not yet learned.” By this he meant the monk’s spiritual wisdom and moral excellence.

St. Arsenius frequently reminded himself, “O Arsenius, remember the purpose for which you left the world.” Thus he spent many nights in tears, weeping so much that the hairs of his eyelashes fell out.

Once the most finely dressed man in the imperial court, he became after his monastic vow the least concerned with appearances. He ate sparingly, labored with his hands, and when he attended church, he always stood hidden behind a particular pillar.

When Pope Theophilus, the 23rd Patriarch, wished to visit him, he sent a messenger ahead. The saint replied, “Tell the Pope: ‘If you come, I will open my door to you. But if I open it for you, I will no longer be able to close it to anyone. And if I open my door to everyone, I cannot remain here.’” St. Arsenius excelled in the virtue of silence for which he is remembered for his famous saying: “I have often repented of having spoken, but never of having been silent.”

St. Arsenius witnessed the first Berber raid on the wilderness of Shiheet in 407 A.D. In 411 A.D. he went to Canopus, soon after he returned to Scetis, where he remained until 432 A.D. Because of further raids, he left the desert and took refuge in a monastery on Mount Torah—later known as the Monastery of El-Kosair or the Monastery of Heraclius—Also known as the Monastery of the mule-where he lived for ten years. In 442 A.D. he was again forced to leave due to Berber incursions and went to Canopus for three years, then returned once more to Mount Torah. There he spent his final two years and departed in peace in 447 A.D.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-13.title: The Departure of St. Arsenius, the Tutor of the Emperor's Children

09-13.html:
On this day also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) the Saint Abba Pigol (Begoul) the Soldier, was martyred. This saint was born in the city of Tala, el-Minya governorate to godly parents and he was inclined since his young age to a life of chastity.

When he enlisted in the army, he spent his salary on the poor and the needy. He persevered on the life of vigils, praises, continuous fasting and prayers, serving the infirm and the prisoners.

The saint left the army and went to the wilderness which was west of Tala to dedicate his life to prayers and worship. He went every Saturday to the nearby church, spent the night in praising God then partook of the holy mysteries by the hand of St. Pigol.

The angel of the Lord appeared to him, strengthened and encouraged the saint and told him that he would be martyred. He went to Alexandria and declared his faith before Armanius the governor. He ordered to scourge him until his bones were exposed. The Lord sent his angel who healed him. The governor became angry so he placed him on an iron bed and lit fire under but the fire became like cold dew. When the governor became weary of tormenting him, he sent him to Arianus, governor of Ansena, who tortured him with the Hinbazeen. His face was shining and his body was filled with strength. When Arianus saw that he cried out saying; “I will see who can save you from my hand.” He ordered to pull out the nails of his hands and legs, to beat him with an iron spout, to hang him on a tall mast, head down, then cut the rope so he would fall on his head and die however the angel of the Lord saved him. Many of the people of Ansena believed.

Arianus sent him to Emperor Diocletian in Antioch where he again confessed the Lord Christ before him. He ordered to imprison him where he was visited by St. Victor Ebn Romanus. Many miracles took place in prison which enraged the emperor. He ordered to cast him in a dark pit and to cover it with a heavy rock to die therein. The next morning the soldier found his arms spread out praying so the emperor ordered him beheaded thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-13.title: The Martyrdom of the Saint Abba Pigol (Begoul) the Soldier

09-14.html:
On this day of the year 64 of the martyrs (348 A.D.), Abba Pachomius, the father of the spiritual monastic communal life (Cenobitic life), departed. This Holy Father was born in Thebes (Luxor) to pagan parents about the year 290 A.D. He loved since his young age the life of purity and chastity. He rejected pagan worship and refused to participate in its feasts. His father once took him to offer a sacrifice to the devils which were in the river. When a pagan priest saw him, shouted out saying; “Keep away the enemy of the gods from here so they would cease their anger from us.”

He was recruited in the Roman army. On his way with several other youth to subdue a revolt against the emperor by the king of Ethiopia, they rested at the shore of the city of Latopolis (Esna). Its people came out and offered them food and drink generously with joy. Pachomius asked about the reason of their kindness. He was told that they do this for the sake of the God of heaven. He decided to become a Christian if he returned safely. With divine providence the revolt was abated and the soldiers were discharged.

The saint went to Dandara where he registered his name in the catechumen’s list. Then he was baptized by the hand of Anba Serapion bishop of Dandara in the year 314 A.D. He remained about three years performing deeds of charity and mercy and his heart was inflamed with the desire of consecration. He went to the saint Anba Balamon (Palaemon) where he became a monk and stayed for seven years in obedience and submission to him. He mastered well the ways of the monastic life.

Then the angel of the Lord appeared to him and commanded him to establish the system of the monastic communal life. He told his teacher Anba Balamon about the command of the angel. He was exceedingly happy, blessed the project and went with him to Tabennesi. He aided Abba Pachomius in establishing the first monastery. Then he bid him farewell to return to his cave with the agreement to meet once a year.

Soon after, many joined the communal monasticism so St. Pachomius built for them ten monasteries. His older brother John came, became a monk under his guidance and assisted him in establishing the monasteries. His sister also came to him; he encouraged her on the monastic life, and built for her a convent east of the Nile that housed about three hundred nuns.

He had all the monasteries under one system of manual labor, certain times for communal prayers and as of fasting, the monk ate twice a day. He was the father of all the monasteries and appointed an Abbot in each monastery. He visited the monasteries and their monks regularly to oversee their affairs. Anba Pachomius refused the priestly ranks in the monasteries. When Pope Athanasius wanted to ordain him a priest, he fled away from him. The Pope told his children the monks; “Tell your father, he who built his house on the rock that can’t be shaken, and fled from the vainglory of the world, is blessed, and his disciples are also blessed.” When he was assured that the Pope will not ordain him, he received him on his way back from Aswan with great joy.

The saint opened the doors of the cenobitic monasteries to the non-Egyptian from the Greeks, Romans and others and each of these groups had a leader over it. He allowed the solitary life for those who desired it.

The saint was known for his meekness and humility. One of the brethren asked him to describe for him one of the spiritual visions and he replied saying; “If you see a meek and humble brother do not seek any other sight. The saint loved his children but he was also firm.

He remained the father of the Cenobitic monasteries until the spread of Plague in Egypt. The saint went around the ill monks with plague to minister unto them. While he was attending the prayers of the feast of Ascension he felt the signs of this evil illness in his body. After the end of the service he called his disciples and appointed for them St. Petronius to be the head of the monasteries after him, then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-14.title: The Departure of St. Pachomius (Pakhom), the Father of the Spiritual Communal Monastic life (Cenobitic life)

09-14.html:
On this day also of the year 250 A.D. St. Epimachus of Pelusium was martyred. He was born in Farma (Pelusium) and he worked as a weaver. He was gentle, quiet and loving the life of contemplation. He often went to the wilderness nearby el-Farma longing for the life of asceticism and worship however he received the crown of martyrdom instead of this angelic life.

When he heard about the horrific torment that the Christian suffered in Alexandria, he decided to go to meet the governor. He travelled to Alexandria and went to the courtyard with his peasant clothes, knocking down a pagan altar of incense and admonished the magistrate for his savagery. The soldiers jumped over him, scourged him, chained the saint with fetters and cast him in prison. He comforted the confessors and encouraged them to be steadfast in the faith which exasperated the magistrate more. When he came before the court he confessed the Lord Christ. The ruler ordered to hang him naked and scourged until his flesh was torn. Then he ordered him be squeezed by the Hinbazeen, he bled and a drop of his blood fell on the eyes of a blind child and she received her sight. Her family believed in the Lord Christ and received the crown of martyrdom. That enraged the governor who ordered to behead the saint. When the executioner drew his sword all power left him and he was unable to strike, and so with fourteen other executioners who all tried to behead St. Epimachus. When they failed to behead him, tied a rope around his neck and was dragged until he delivered his spirit in the hand of the Lord and received the crown of martyrdom.

A deaf person carried his body to cast it away, when he touched the body his ears were opened and was able to hear. Some believers from Edko came, took the body and shrouded it. A church was built after his name in el-Farma to which the body was relocated.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-14.title: The Martyrdom of St. Epimachus (Ephimachus) of Pelusium

09-15.html:
On this day of the year 68 A.D. St. Simon the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles, was martyred.
